body.statement: Under \(\operatorname{rank}(C)=d\), a finite breakout can occur only if \(E\ge d+2\).  If \(E=d+1\), then \(A=\mathbb R^d\) and \(Q_A=0\).  Conversely, for every \(d\ge1\), \(E\ge d+2\), and \(R_{\max}\ge d+2\), there exist finite \(M\), positive \(\kappa_0\), and one fixed choice of the remaining bounds such that, for every \(r\in\{d+2,\ldots,R_{\max}\}\), centered independent entire-mgf source laws satisfy those same bounds and calibration gap with \(r^\star=r\).
body.justification: The environment count is an exact resource threshold once the latent profile dimension is fixed.
body.gap: BACKSHIFT's three-setting threshold concerns covariance joint diagonalization; the proposed \(d+2\) threshold concerns a selected confounded effect and includes realizability at every prescribed higher order.
body.consumer: The result tells experimentalists how many perturbation environments are minimally required to leave a \(d\)-factor latent-shift geometry.
body.proof_tex:
The columns of \(C\) lie in \(\mathbb R^{E-1}\).  Thus \(\operatorname{rank}(C)=d\) implies \(d\leq E-1\).  If \(E=d+1\), then \(C\) has rank \(d\) in \(\mathbb R^d\), so
\[
 A=\operatorname{col}(C)=\mathbb R^d,
 \qquad Q_A=0.                                      \tag{13}
\]
Consequently no projected contrast can be nonzero.  More generally, a finite breakout requires \(A^\perp\neq\{0\}\), hence \(d<E-1\), which is equivalent to \(E\geq d+2\).

We now prove attainability at every prescribed order with one collection of bounds.  Fix \(d\geq1\), \(E\geq d+2\), and \(R_{\max}\geq d+2\).  For \(r\in\{d+2,\ldots,R_{\max}\}\), define
\[
 \nu_{rj}=(-1)^{r-j}\binom{r}{j},\qquad 1\leq j\leq r.
\]
The binomial identity
\[
 \sum_{j=0}^r(-1)^{r-j}\binom{r}{j}e^{jt}=(e^t-1)^r                 \tag{14}
\]
shows, after taking \(k\) derivatives at zero, that
\[
 \sum_{j=1}^r\nu_{rj}j^k=0\quad(0\leq k<r),
 \qquad
 \sum_{j=1}^r\nu_{rj}j^r=r!.                       \tag{15}
\]
The omitted \(j=0\) term is zero for \(k\geq1\), and (15) at \(k=0\) follows directly from (14).

Choose \(L,\eta>0\), put
\[
 K_\nu=\max_{d+2\leq s\leq R_{\max}}\max_{1\leq j\leq s}|\nu_{sj}|,
 \qquad 0<\varepsilon<L/(2K_\nu),                    \tag{16}
\]
and use the environment \(e=d+1\) as a spare coordinate.  Let \(\epsilon_{u,e}\) be a centered compound-Poisson sum having jumps \(1,\ldots,d\), baseline intensity \(L\) at every jump, and, only in environment \(e=j\leq d\), an additional intensity \(\eta\) at jump \(j\).  Add an independent centered Gaussian if desired.  Let \(\epsilon_{t,e}\) have jumps \(1,\ldots,R_{\max}\), all with baseline intensity \(L\), except that in the spare environment its jump-\(j\) intensity is \(L+\varepsilon\nu_{rj}\) for \(j\leq r\).  Again add a common independent Gaussian.  All remaining environments have baseline intensities.  Inequality (16) makes every intensity at least \(L/2>0\).  Take \(\epsilon_y\) Gaussian and all source families mutually independent, and set \(\alpha=1\), \(\beta=0\), and \(\gamma=1\).

The compound-Poisson log moment generating function calculation used above and (15) give
\[
 u_k=\eta(1^k,\ldots,d^k,0,\ldots,0)^\top,
 \qquad
 c_k=u_k+\varepsilon\!\left(\sum_{j=1}^r\nu_{rj}j^k\right)\mathbf e_{d+1}. \tag{17}
\]
Because \(r\geq d+2\), equations (15)--(17) imply
\[
 C=\begin{bmatrix}\eta V_d\\0\end{bmatrix},
 \quad
 A=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf e_1,\ldots,\mathbf e_d\},
 \quad
 Q_Ac_k=0\ (d+2\leq k<r),
 \quad
 Q_Ac_r=\varepsilon r!\,\mathbf e_{d+1}\neq0.        \tag{18}
\]
The polynomial-root argument in the proof of the nonvacuity proposition proves that \(V_d\) is nonsingular.  Hence the calibration rank is \(d\), and
\[
 \sigma_d(C)=\eta\sigma_d(V_d)>0.                    \tag{19}
\]
Equations (18)--(19) prove \(r^\star=r\) and the latent-profile restriction at every order.

All sources are centered and independent, and their moment generating functions are entire.  There are only finitely many values of \(r\), environments, and source families in the construction.  Therefore their absolute moments of order \(2R_{\max}+\delta\) have a finite maximum.  Choose \(M\) larger than that maximum and choose
\[
 0<\kappa_0<\eta\sigma_d(V_d).
\]
Choose once and for all coefficient bounds containing \((\alpha,\beta,\gamma)=(1,0,1)\), and choose all other fixed bounds large enough to contain the displayed finite family.  These choices do not depend on \(r\).  Thus the same finite \(M\), positive \(\kappa_0\), and remaining bounds make every construction legal, which proves the converse and hence sharpness.
